title: Do the SKY130 area and latency conclusions for a MAC-engine family survive a target clock period?
summary: eda-sky130rung mapped each of 40 MAC-engine designs with an unconstrained ABC map, so each ran at its own clock. Here every design is mapped at six shared targets (3–10 ns, map -D T; upsize; dnsize, Yosys 0.33, SKY130 HD tt 25 °C) plus the baseline, 280 mappings. Cell count still ranks area (Spearman 0.995–0.996 at every setting). Logic depth ranks delay at only 0.34–0.82 depending on T, never reliably. No design reaches 3 ns; 6, 15, 25, 39 and 40 of 40 meet 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 ns. With one shared clock the feasible (area, cycles) front equals the generic front (p8, p4, p2, p1 at 4 bits; p8 drops out at 4 ns), and p4w4 is the best area × latency design at every feasible T, so the front change reported with per-design clocks came from the clocks, not the cell library. Limits: ABC combinational delay only (no wires, clock tree or placement), one family, one recipe, no place and route, so none of it is sign-off or silicon.
lede: the 40 MAC-engine designs mapped to SKY130 at six shared clock targets: cell count still ranks area (Spearman 0.995+), logic depth ranks delay at only 0.34 to 0.82, and with one shared clock the Pareto front equals the generic one, so the earlier front change came from per-design clocks.
